conviction_note: Four quarters running, CareDx has raised revenue guidance ($420-444M, then $447-465M, then $490-500M) on beats driven partly by $14-16M a quarter of prior-period collections. The H2 guide appears to assume less of that collection catch-up than Q1 and Q2 delivered. Against that, the stock is up about 57% since the last print, sits at its 52-week high above most price targets, and the whisper ($0.27 vs $0.24) already expects a beat. So the lean is a modest up (p_up 57) on a large unsigned move (15%, the option-implied 15.84%). The findings sum (+3.4) is above the scaled number (+2.1) because the scaled number puts the run-up and sell-the-news risk into p_up.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $122.4M and non-GAAP EPS $0.24 (whisper $0.27), per Earnings Whispers via Finviz 2026-10-21 (https://finviz.com/news/406024/caredx-faces-first-navdx-quarter-with-street-estimates-trailing-its-raised-outlook). Benzinga shows $121.9M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CDNA/earnings-forecasts), so two sources agree. The company guide gives the same figure: FY2026 $490-500M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001217234/000121723426000045/cdna-20260730_earningsrele.htm) less H1 $249.6M (Q1 $117.7M + Q2 $131.9M) leaves $240-250M for H2, about $120-125M a quarter. The bar sits at the guide midpoint. Earnings Whispers' FY consensus of $455M is below the guide floor and looks stale, so it is not used.
positioning_check: Short interest was 6,715,367 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement. That is about 13.0% of 51.73M shares outstanding, 4.49 days to cover. It has risen for four straight settlements: 5.79M on 08-14, 5.83M on 08-31, 6.30M on 09-15, 6.59M on 09-30 and 6.72M on 10-15. Source: https://equibles.com/stocks/cdna/shortinterest. The skew is null in the baseline (skew_25d_vol_points null). Put/call open interest is 2.0 on 10,773 contracts, and the ATM spread is 46% of mid, so the implied move is indicative only. The tape: spot $72.26 at its 52-week high and 406% off the low, up 9.1% over 20 days and 4.5% over 5. MarketBeat's average target is $54 (3 Buy / 5 Hold) and S&P Global's is $61.67 (7 analysts). The highest is BTIG at $74.

findings.finding: CareDx booked about $14M of prior-period revenue in Q1 and $15.6M in Q2 from improved collections. The H2 guide appears to assume much less. Call coverage puts FY testing services at about $400M including $24M of H2 oncology. With H1 testing at $191.3M, that leaves about $185M of transplant testing in H2, roughly $92M a quarter. Q2 transplant testing excluding prior-period revenue was $84M, so the guide embeds only about $8M a quarter of catch-up or ASP uplift. At Q2's run rate, Q3 revenue would be about $128-132M against the $122.4M bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-30, amc): revenue $131.9M vs $114.1M consensus (+15.7%), with $16M prior-period revenue and a guide raise; stock +14.72%. Q1 2026 (2026-04-28): $117.7M with $14M prior-period revenue; stock -5.07% on the full report after a +27.6% move on 2026-04-16. Q4 2025 was pre-released on 2026-01-12 (+20.08%) and the full report on 2026-02-24 drew -4.1%. The non-prelim beats were bought; the full reports after a prelim were sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $122.4M sits on the guide midpoint, as if prior-period collections stop. If the market expected collections to continue, the published bar would sit near $128-132M, not at the guide. The whisper EPS ($0.27 vs $0.24) shows the buy side leans toward a beat, so part of this is priced. Prior-period revenue is also lower-quality revenue that the market may discount.
findings.independence: The Q1 release (https://www.caredx.com/newsroom/press-releases/caredx-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial-results) shows the same pattern, about $14M prior-period revenue tied to collections. That is the same company's own documents, not an independent series. The $400M testing-services and $24M oncology figures come from call-summary aggregators, not the transcript.

findings.finding: CareDx has raised its FY revenue guide at every print this year: $420-444M (Jan), $447-465M (Apr 28), $490-500M (Jul 30). With H1 at $249.6M and the bar at the guide midpoint, a Q3 near $128M+ makes a fourth raise likely, to about $500M+. Q3 is also the first quarter with NavDx in and Lab Products out, so the guide gets re-based in this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Jul 30 guide raise ($447-465M to $490-500M, a +8% midpoint lift) was bought +14.72%. The Apr 28 raise came after an Apr 16 jump and drew -5.07%.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar ($122.4M) equals the current guide midpoint, so a raise is not in the published estimates. But the stock has run +57% since the last print, which suggests the buy side already expects a raise. A small raise could therefore disappoint. The size is held below finding 1's high case for that reason.
findings.independence: This shares the H1 arithmetic with finding 1, so the two are not independent: a raise follows from the beat. The separate input is the Sep 24 BTIG note after Boston investor meetings with the CEO and CFO, which described management as 'confident' late in the quarter (https://www.tikr.com/blog/caredx-14-on-fresh-74-analyst-price-target).

findings.finding: The final MolDX LCD for transplant rejection testing (finalized mid-July 2026, effective 2026-08-30) puts about one month of Q3 under the new rules. It raises kidney surveillance limits to 6 tests in year 1 and 4 a year in years 2-3 (the draft allowed 4 and 2). It removes the proposed HeartCare bundling. It keeps a rule against paying for surveillance within a month of a for-cause test, and the one-service-per-encounter principle. CareDx says the final rule removed about $7.5M of coverage headwind from its guide. Q3 brings the first ordering and billing evidence under the LCD.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The LCD finalization on 2026-07-16 moved the stock from about $30 to $38 (+27%) per the Discoveries in Health Policy write-up. That reaction is not in the baseline's 8-K list because it was not an earnings release.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the July move and the guide raise already reflect the rule. What remains is commentary on Q4 and 2027 ordering under the new limits, and whether the for-cause carve-out or one-service-per-encounter clips HeartCare billing.
findings.independence: Natera's release on the same LCD lists the same test limits (https://www.natera.com/company/news/finalized-moldx-lcd-includes-expanded-coverage-for-nateras-prospera-portfolio/). The Earnings Whispers preview reports the $7.5M headwind removal (https://finviz.com/news/406024/caredx-faces-first-navdx-quarter-with-street-estimates-trailing-its-raised-outlook).

findings.finding: The FY adjusted EBITDA guide of $66-78M, less H1 (about $19M + $24.8M), implies only $22-34M across H2, about $11-17M a quarter, against $24.8M in Q2. Earnings Whispers attributes the gap to NavDx integration costs and conservative oncology pricing ($770-795 a test vs the $1,800 Medicare rate, with a Q4 billing migration aimed at $1,000+). A Q3 EBITDA well above $11-17M would beat a lowballed profit guide. This is net of the Lab Products EBITDA that left with the divestiture.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's EBITDA of $24.8M (19% margin, vs $5.3M a year earlier) came with the +14.72% reaction. EBITDA was not separable from the revenue beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The published EPS bar of $0.24 vs $0.37 in Q2 shows the street has taken the guide's H2 profit step-down at face value. If the market expected Q2-level EBITDA, the EPS bar would be nearer $0.35. The whisper of $0.27 moves only a little way toward that.
findings.independence: The guide figures come from the company's 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001217234/000121723426000045/cdna-20260730_earningsrele.htm). The pricing figures come from the Earnings Whispers preview only. Same company documents; no independent series.

findings.finding: Short interest has risen four settlements in a row while the stock roughly doubled, from 5.79M shares (08-14) to 6.72M (10-15). That is about 13% of shares outstanding, 4.5 days to cover, so a beat-and-raise meets a growing short base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On non-prelim beats the stock moved +14.72% (2026-07-30) and +13.84% (2025-11-04), consistent with short covering amplifying good prints. On misses it moved -7.86% (2025-08-06) and -10.72% (2025-04-30).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, but a short base that keeps growing into a stock at its highs means part of the market positioned for a disappointment. If the shorts had been squeezed already, SI would have fallen across the run, and it rose.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print at $72.26, its 52-week high. That is up about 57% since the Jul 30 print (about $46 on Aug 4-5 per the insider sale prices), up 13% since $64.00 on Oct 16, and above the MarketBeat average target of $54 and the S&P Global average of $61.67, with only BTIG ($74) above spot. The whisper is above consensus. A merely in-line beat-and-raise could be sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prints that followed a large pre-print move were sold: -5.07% (2026-04-28, after +27.6% on 04-16) and -4.1% (2026-02-24, after +20.08% on 01-12). This run-up is a drift, not a single prelim jump, so the analogy is partial.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a positioning fact rather than unpriced information. It is the bar the print has to clear. If the run-up did not already embed a beat and raise, the whisper would not sit above consensus and the stock would not sit above most targets.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview notes shares up about 63% since the last report and more than double the 200-day average (https://finviz.com/news/406024/caredx-faces-first-navdx-quarter-with-street-estimates-trailing-its-raised-outlook). MarketBeat gives the $54 average target (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-caredx-nasdaq-cdna-shares-up-6-still-a-buy-2026-10-13/).

findings.finding: Natera, the direct competitor in transplant cfDNA, got the same LCD expansion for Prospera. On its Q2 call (2026-08-06) management tied it to expected Prospera ASP and volume gains. Underlying transplant procedures are flat: CareDx called them roughly flat, and 2025 US kidney transplants fell by 116 to 28,377. CareDx's growth therefore depends on surveillance penetration against a better-funded rival with equal coverage.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history in the baseline on competitive-share commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy, not a CareDx number. Natera reports Q3 after this window, so no fresh competitor data has arrived since CareDx last spoke. It matters only if CareDx's Q3 volume misses its own 58,000 transplant-test target.
findings.independence: Kidney Transplant Collaborative 2025 data via HealthDay (https://www.healthday.com/health-news/general-health/mistrust-fuels-drop-in-deceased-organ-donations-kidney-transplants). This is a proxy for procedures, not for CareDx's share.

The Q4 2026 NavDx billing migration toward $1,000+ a test (vs $770-795 assumed) would affect Q4 and 2027, not the Q3 print. It enters this window only through commentary.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew. Put/call OI of 2.0 and a 52-week-high spot after a +57% run since the last print cut against the long lean from the beat-and-raise arithmetic, and that tension is why p_up is 57 rather than the 60s that the guide-vs-collections evidence alone would support.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs and beat quality): finding 1 rests on prior-period collection revenue, a catch-up item. Its size went from +3.0 to +2.0 because the market can discount PPR-driven beats; the path to the guide is kept in finding 2.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction) together with the run-up: p_up went from 58 to 57, so expected_move fell from 2.4 to 2.1. abs_move_pct stays at 15 (lesson 8: do not shrink).
Lesson 6 (bar): the bar was checked against two agreeing sources ($122.4M, $121.9M) and the guide midpoint, so no cap was applied.

Lessons 3, 5, 7 and 9 left the other findings standing: the proxy (finding 7) was already small, the positioning findings do not contradict each other, and the NavDx/EBITDA finding is already net of the Lab Products exit.
